correctness.rationale: The proof conditions one Dirichlet coordinate above a threshold, rescales the remaining simplex, and computes the conditional Greenwood mean from standard Dirichlet moments. Exchangeability then gives the covariance with the exceedance count, and the empirical-CDF covariance follows by an affine transformation. The variance formula follows from exact one- and two-coordinate exceedance probabilities. The asymptotic variance uses a one-order expansion of the joint-exceedance term; the zero-integral identity follows pathwise from the fact that the spacings sum to one. Exact rational checks independently reproduce the finite formulas on a broad threshold grid. No finite grid is used as proof of the all-threshold theorem.

value.rationale: Both Greenwood's statistic and empirical spacing distributions are classical goodness-of-fit diagnostics. The theorem identifies how a global quadratic dispersion measure couples to each local spacing threshold, including an exact sign change near twice the mean spacing, a nonvanishing fixed-threshold asymptotic correlation, and a zero-area compensation law. This is a structural joint-distribution fact rather than a marginal-moment recomputation or an arbitrary numerical slice.
